keyword: did the artemis 2 land on the moon

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission did not land on the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "they didn’t land on it. Instead, the astronauts on the Artemis II mission flew around the moon" (R1); "fly around the moon" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state or strongly imply no landing occurred, describing the mission as a flyby or trip around the moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission had four astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four astronauts headed back to the moon" (R1); "All four astronauts" (R2); "The four Artemis II astronauts" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All sources consistently name or refer to exactly four astronauts by name or count.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II astronauts performed a flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe the mission as a lunar flyby.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II astronauts orbited the moon before returning to Earth.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "crewed lunar flyby" (R1); "fly around the moon" (R2); "flying around the moon" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe a flyby trajectory around the moon, not entry into lunar orbit (which requires orbit insertion burn); no source states they orbited.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II astronauts splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "scheduled to splash down on the evening of April 10 off the coast of San Diego" (R1); "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean at 5.07pm PT after a 10-day journey" (R2); "splashdown off the coast of San Diego... April 10, 2026" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm safe splashdown on exact date in Pacific Ocean.

verifications.claim: Artemis II was the first crewed mission to orbit the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "crewed lunar flyby" (R1); "first humans to travel to the moon... since the Apollo 17 mission of December 1972" (R2); no mention of orbiting the Moon (flyby instead)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 (1972), but specify flyby not orbit; Apollo 17 did orbit and land.

verifications.claim: The goal of the Artemis II mission was to test the Orion spacecraft's systems with a crew on a ~10-day journey.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "critical and necessary test of NASA’s deep-space systems... verify Orion’s life support systems... 10-day mission" (R1); "10-day journey to fly around the moon" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state testing Orion systems with crew on ~10-day mission.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew flew around the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "new photos of moon's far side... flew around the moon" (R1); "around the far side of the moon" (R2); "first humans to see the entire lunar far side" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm travel around and views/photos of the far side.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew set a record for the farthest humans have ever traveled into space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "breaking the record set by Apollo 13 in 1970... traveled the farthest from Earth than any humans ever before" (R1); "set a new record for the farthest distance from Earth any humans have ever traveled: 252,756 miles" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state distance record broken vs. Apollo 13.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean near San Diego.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splash down... off the coast of San Diego, California" (R1); "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean... off the coast of San Diego" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: All splashdown reports confirm safe landing in Pacific near San Diego.

verifications.claim: A future Artemis mission (Artemis III or later) is planned for a lunar surface landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis III... test... needed to land astronauts on the Moon... early 2028, Artemis IV mission's goal is to land humans on the moon" (R1); "next lunar landing in 2028" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail plans for Artemis III/IV lunar landings.
